Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our annotated order form with a few redlines called out. High level items for us:

- Output ownership: we need explicit language that customer retains ownership of customer-provided content and that generated outputs used to power Brightline product features remain exclusively Brightline's IP.
- Training/data use: we cannot allow any model retraining or telemetry ingestion that includes PHI or identifiable patient data; where non-PHI logs are used, we need an explicit opt-in, retention limits, and deletion rights.
- Feedback license: we want a narrowly scoped feedback license (read-only, nonexclusive, non-transferable) limited to product safety/bug fixes — no rights to use for model training or commercial re-use.

I added inline comments in Brightline_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.docx. Can you route this to legal and procurement on your side? We'd like an internal response by end of week if possible; procurement has a go-live target of 12/15 so timing is tight.

Team / Olivia — I reviewed Brightline_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.docx and summarized material points below. I used "Company" to mean Brightline and "Redwood" for us.

Summary of our position and suggested language:

1) Output ownership (customer-generated outputs) - We can agree that Brightline owns outputs that are direct derivatives of Customer Data and that are necessary for their product feature. However, we need a carveback that allows Redwood to use non-identifying aggregated outputs for safety/quality monitoring and to improve inference services — explicitly prohibiting any use for model training unless Brightline provides opt-in written consent. Suggested clause: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and Outputs generated directly from Customer Data. Redwood may only use aggregated, de-identified Output telemetry for service safety and reliability; Redwood shall not use Customer Data or Outputs for model training without Customer's written consent."

2) Training/data use and telemetry - We are aligned on zero-tolerance for PHI. Propose to add a definition for "Sensitive Data" that includes PHI and require an explicit operational flow: separate logging endpoint for sensitive vs non-sensitive requests, retention periods, and deletion on request. Also include evidence: Redwood will provide the SOC2 controls and an architecture diagram showing telemetry separation.

3) Feedback license (scoped) - Recommend a narrow feedback license for bug fixes and safety improvements that is time-limited (12 months) and non-sublicensable. Reject any open-ended perpetual feedback license that permits model retraining.

4) Audit & evidence requests - We will provide a runbook and sample logs in a sealed evidence package (redacted) via secure share. Any full log sharing will require a data transfer agreement specific to the dataset.

5) Pricing/operational impact - Ben/Markus: if we accept the opt-in model-training restriction, we need CLARITY on how training exceptions (customer-paid retrain engagements) will be priced and scoped — propose a separate SOW for any custom retrain. Also need to confirm if Brightline expects attribution/attribution removal for downstream productization.

- Sean to confirm negotiation strategy with Sales leadership — Thu 11/12.
